description: FRED (Federal Reserve Economic Data) is an online database of economic time series gathered from national, international, public and private sources, covering interest rates, exchange rates, money, banking and credit, prices, production, employment, trade and regional indicators. It is run by the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, which has provided it since 1991. Coverage is mainly the United States, down to state, county and metropolitan areas, with many international series; frequencies range from daily, such as exchange rates, to annual, and series are updated continuously as sources release data. Data can be graphed, downloaded, pulled through the FRED API and an Excel add-in, or embedded as widgets, free of charge. Caveats: FRED re-publishes other agencies' series, so definitions, revisions and copyright follow each source, and the home page read does not state a single licence. For simulation it supplies macroeconomic and financial time series used to calibrate and test stress scenarios, to measure the economic footprint of disasters and infrastructure outages, and to drive resilience models of the financial sector. It is related to the Federal Reserve G.17 industrial production record in this catalogue, whose series FRED also serves.
